sources.entry: Audiobookshelf - Audiobook and podcast server. It streams all audio formats, keeps and syncs progress across devices. Comes with apps for Android and iOS. (Source Code, Clients) GPL-3.0 Docker/deb/Nodejs

summary.one_liner: Audiobookshelf Mobile App is the Android and iOS client (built with NuxtJS and Capacitor) for the self-hosted Audiobookshelf audiobook and podcast server.
summary.what_it_does: This repository contains the mobile client for Audiobookshelf, a self-hosted audiobook and podcast server. The app requires an Audiobookshelf server to connect with and does not work standalone. The README describes a single codebase built with NuxtJS and Capacitor that targets both Android and iOS. It explains how to set up the development environment on Windows and macOS, install npm packages, generate the static web app, and sync it into the native Android and iOS projects. The README does not list specific playback or sync features; the awesome-selfhosted listing describes streaming all audio formats and syncing progress across devices. Localization is handled through Weblate.
use_cases: Listen to audiobooks from a self-hosted server on Android
Listen to podcasts from a self-hosted server on iOS
Develop or contribute to the Audiobookshelf mobile app
Build the Android or iOS app from source with Capacitor
Help translate Audiobookshelf into other languages
how_to_run: Install Node.js 20, Android Studio or Xcode, and Cocoapods as needed
git clone the repository and cd into the project directory
npx cap open android (or npx cap open ios); after JS changes, run npm run sync
notable: One codebase for both Android and iOS via Capacitor
Client for the self-hosted Audiobookshelf server
Setup instructions for both Windows and macOS
caveats: Requires an Audiobookshelf server; it is only a client
The iOS app is in early beta and the TestFlight beta is currently full, per the README
The Android app is in beta
keywords: listen to audiobooks from my server
